projects.title: Customer Review Sentiment Analysis
projects.short: From pizza reviews to sentiment patterns. Exploring recurrent models through text preprocessing, tuning and baseline comparison.
projects.problem: Explore how recurrent neural networks can classify sentiment in pizza reviews, and how a BiGRU model compares with an RNN baseline.
projects.contribution: I built RNN and BiGRU models, preprocessed the review text, tuned the models and evaluated performance against the RNN baseline.
approach: Preprocess the review text for model input.
Build and tune recurrent models using Python, TensorFlow and Keras.
Evaluate the BiGRU model against the RNN baseline.
projects.evidence: The project work includes text preprocessing, model tuning and baseline evaluation. The diagram below illustrates that workflow; it is not a model output.
projects.limitation: Accuracy and F1 results are not published here. A baseline comparison is the focus of this study; the available evidence does not establish performance on new domains or deployment readiness.
projects.learning: The learning objective was to connect text preparation, recurrent architecture choices and evaluation in one sentiment-analysis workflow.

projects.title: Graduate Employment & Salary Trends
projects.short: Exploring graduate outcomes across institutions from 2018–2023, with salary comparisons and a closer look at employment cohorts.
projects.problem: Explore how graduate salary and employment patterns vary across institutions and years, including fresh and post–National Service graduates.
projects.contribution: My contribution focused on salary trends and exceptions across institutions, employment patterns by institution, and comparisons between fresh and post–National Service graduates. The shared dashboard labels these panels with my name; other panels were created by a teammate.
approach: Use Power BI to compare salary trends across institutions from 2018–2023.
Examine employment patterns across institutions and employment types.
Compare outcomes for fresh and post–National Service graduates.
projects.evidence: Original group dashboard. Caden-labelled panels show my contribution; the whole dashboard is shared group work. Open the full image to inspect the labels.
projects.limitation: These are descriptive comparisons, not evidence that institution or National Service status causes an outcome. Aggregated figures depend on the selected year and cohort; no business-impact claim is made.
projects.learning: The learning objective was to make differences between institutions and cohorts easier to examine through visual comparison.

projects.title: SQL ETL & Data Warehouse
projects.short: Organising library loan data into a MySQL star-schema warehouse, from cleaning and transformation to borrowing-pattern queries.
projects.problem: Organise library loan data into a structure that supports analysis of borrowing patterns.
projects.contribution: I designed a MySQL star-schema warehouse, cleaned and transformed data through ETL, and wrote SQL queries to analyse borrowing patterns.
approach: Design a star-schema warehouse for library loan data.
Clean and transform data through an ETL workflow.
Write SQL queries to explore borrowing patterns.
projects.evidence: The workflow illustration summarises the project stages. It is not a screenshot of the database or an exact schema diagram.
projects.limitation: The schema, query files and measured results are not published here. No dataset size, speed improvement or validation statistics are claimed.
projects.learning: The learning objective was to connect data modelling and ETL with SQL analysis in a warehouse workflow.

projects.title: Analogy Tutor
projects.short: A learning-interface prototype for query, key and value concepts, with separate scripted and generated reply modes.
projects.problem: Explore how analogies can introduce query, key and value concepts, with a clear distinction between a fixed teaching example and a generated explanation.
projects.contribution: This repository brings together a browser learning interface and an Express backend. The implementation separates scripted replies from generated replies, manages conversation sessions, and handles provider errors. These are source-verified implementation details; live model behaviour has not been validated for this portfolio.
approach: Offer explicitly selected scripted and generated reply modes.
Route requests through Express with separate in-memory conversation sessions.
Use a server-side Groq API provider for generated replies, with structured response validation and timeout handling.
projects.evidence: The linked source contains the session and chat routes in server.js and a real model API request in server/groq-provider.js. Scripted mode uses a separate provider. The workflow below is illustrative.
projects.limitation: This is a prototype. Generated mode requires a configured backend API key; it is not hosted inside this static portfolio. No live model request was tested during this redesign, and generated explanations may be inaccurate. Interactive graphics are separate from reply generation.
projects.learning: The learning focus is the boundary between interface behaviour, deterministic teaching content and model-generated responses.
